title: You do not call it evil.
paragraphs:
You do not call it evil.
You call it understandable.
That is how the heart hides.
Isaiah 5:20 does not whisper. It warns: “Woe to those who call evil good and good evil.”

Not those who accidentally stumbled.
Those who renamed sin so they could sleep beside it.

We do it more than we admit.
Bitterness becomes “boundaries.”
Lust becomes “need.”
Pride becomes “confidence.”
Disobedience becomes “peace.”
And what God clearly confronted, we decorate with softer words so conscience stops shouting.

The danger is not only in doing wrong.
The deeper danger is justifying what we already know is wrong.
Because once you baptize rebellion with nice language, repentance starts to feel unnecessary.

Sin does not become safe because culture applauds it.
Darkness does not become light because your feelings defend it.
And a lie does not become truth because you repeated it long enough.
But grace walks in right there.

Jesus did not come for people who had no sin.
He came for people honest enough to stop hiding it.
The cross is not for the self-excused.
It is for the broken, the convicted, the surrendering.
When you call sin what God calls it, you are not losing freedom — you are finally stepping into it.

So stop renaming what God has already revealed.
Drop the excuse.
Break agreement with the lie.
Come clean before the Lord.

There is mercy for the one who repents.
There is cleansing for the one who confesses.
There is no shame too deep that the blood of Jesus cannot wash.

Call it what it is.
Then bring it to Christ.
